intro: Embeddings represent items as vectors. Cosine similarity measures whether two vectors point in the same direction, regardless of their length.
task: Implement `cosine_similarity(a, b)` for two nonempty, finite, one-dimensional vectors of equal length. Return a scalar between -1 and 1.
requirements: Accept numeric lists or NumPy arrays and leave both inputs unchanged.
Return 0.0 if either vector is all zeros; zero has no direction.
Raise ValueError for empty, mismatched, non-1D, or non-finite vectors.
Handle large and tiny finite values without overflowing the norm.

hints.title: Validate first
hints.body: Convert both inputs to float64 arrays. Check their dimensions, sizes, and finiteness.

hints.title: Scale before taking a norm
hints.body: Divide each nonzero vector by its own largest absolute element. This leaves direction unchanged and avoids squared values near 1e616.

hints.title: Normalize and compare
hints.body: Normalize the scaled vectors, take their dot product, then clip roundoff to [-1, 1].

explanation: The dot product combines corresponding coordinates. Dividing by both vector lengths removes magnitude, leaving the cosine of the angle between them.
Scaling a vector by a positive number does not change its direction. Scaling by its largest absolute coordinate before computing a norm keeps arithmetic in a manageable range.
A zero vector has no angle. This exercise adopts an explicit 0.0 convention so later retrieval code can handle empty representations deterministically.
